answer: A logistics market resists Sybils by granting one paid assignment per bonded, GPS-attested vehicle rather than per account. If an agent books a cedar shipment across a bridge into the tundra, it must commit a route plan and signed vehicle telemetry before dispatch. Several names sharing the same vehicle certificate compete for that single slot; impossible simultaneous trips or forged telemetry slash the common bond. Opening extra profiles therefore adds cost but no extra reward.
